TraversalGraph and the Store cannot get there (their rollback cannot fail) (Transactions).
  • Errors that surface now. Failures that used to read as "no data" are errors: an unreadable store directory or single-file store (Store::is_store, SingleFileDir::is_single_file), an unreadable attic or models directory (Store::info), a failing compression estimate (Graph::advise), a read the current thread may not have (GraphError::GraphViewHeld instead of an empty answer), a poisoned internal lock of a Store (StoreFailure::LockPoisoned instead of a default answer). The CLI, the dev server, MCP and Python report them.
  • graphersal-session (internal) returns the typed SessionError instead of String; graphersal-wasm's JS methods throw instead of answering an empty value.
  • Python: Store.close() raises on a poisoned store lock (was "already closed"), Graph.execute raises on a poisoned limits lock (was the default limits). Everything else is unchanged.
  • DSL: a predicate whose operand is a list, map or traversal (P.gt(["a"])) is an error now; it used to compare with the operand's text (issue #14, under "Fixed").

Added

  • Embedding models inside a Store (Embedding Models in a Store, issue #10): graphersal embed-model download <repo> --into <store> and embed-model import <dir> --into <store> put a Model2Vec model into a store, with its model card, its licence files (a standard licence text when the model ships none, and the texts of its base models' licences) and a manifest with a SHA-256 per file. Opening the store registers its models, so a text query embeds with the model the schema recorded wherever the store goes. Every copy carries them (backups, ZIP backups, fork, attic fork, repair, convert, upgrade, restore, packed snapshots); store verify checks every file. graphersal store models lists and removes them, store info shows them, store export and store backup --zip take --without-models. Rust Store::add_model/models/remove_model, Python Store.models() and Store.export(without_models=), the playground's Store menu (downloads with or without models).
  • Units held across locks (Transactions): Graph::begin_unit/commit_unit/commit_unit_with/rollback_unit/discard_unit/ unit_changes/holds_unit keep one unit over several locks on the opening thread. Other threads read on while the unit has only read and wait from its first write until it closes, so nobody sees uncommitted changes. Whole-script units (eval_value_atomic, dry runs, writing saved queries, query jobs) and the playground's and dev server's runs use them: readers are no longer blocked by a script that only reads. Graph::try_write_checked tells "busy" from "forbidden on this thread"; Graph::read_checked/write_checked/try_read report an aliasing view as GraphError::GraphViewHeld instead of panicking.
  • AI Chat export: the AI Chat tab's Export menu downloads the transcript as Markdown or JSON (AI Chat, issue #18). The AI Chat keeps its history compressed, shows the input, output and cached token counts of each answer, and answers from what it has when it reaches the tool-call limit.
  • Storage advisor: every recommendation has an impact (low, medium, high: its share of the graph's memory, or the scans and reads it saves) beside its confidence, and the list is ordered by it (Optimize).
  • Dev server on any address, and in Docker (Listening address and Docker): the dev server (graphersal --server, with --mcp and --ai) has a new --host <ADDR> option to listen on any address (for example --host 0.0.0.0), and inside a Docker or Podman container it now listens on 0.0.0.0 by default, so docker run -p 8080:8080 ... graphersal --server --port 8080 works without flags. A non-loopback address prints a warning that the server has no authentication; on the loopback the Host/Origin checks stay as strict as before, and on a network address they still refuse DNS-rebinding requests. A Kubernetes pod (KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST) counts as a container.
  • Running in Docker and Kubernetes (Running in Docker): a Dockerfile in the repository builds the static graphersal binary into a small distroless image (non-root, HEALTHCHECK, STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM) whose default command serves /data/graph.gstore read-only with a read-only MCP endpoint.
    • Health endpoints: GET/HEAD /healthz (liveness: 200 while the process answers HTTP) and /readyz (readiness: 200 when the graph is loaded, 503 while it loads or the server stops). They take no lock, never wait for a running query and are exempt from the Host/Origin checks, so Kubernetes probes and Docker health checks work in every bind mode. The server listens before the graph loads: during a long Store open /healthz answers 200, /readyz and the API 503.
    • graphersal health [--ready] [--host ADDR] [--port N] [--timeout MS]: the probe for images without curl or wget (exit 0 when the endpoint answers 200, 1 otherwise).
    • SIGTERM: the dev server always stops on SIGINT/SIGTERM, also as PID 1 of a container (where a process without a handler ignores SIGTERM and docker stop waits for its kill): the running query is cancelled, /readyz turns 503, a Store is closed cleanly, and the process exits with 0. As PID 1, a one-shot script and the REPL exit with 130 on them too.
    • --read-only: the served graph refuses every write (queries, schema, catalog, "Save to file"; MCP offers only reading tools), and a Store is loaded without its lock and without writing anything, so a :ro mount, a read-only root file system or a file without write permission works, models included. A Store that cannot be opened for writing falls back to it with a note. Rust: Store::stored_embedders_dir (the models of a store loaded with Store::open_read_only); a single-file store on a read-only file system now reads like one without write permission.
  • Dev server: the start output is grouped in sections (Store, Graph, Embedding models, Server) and names every embedding model with its repository, licence and source; the playground shows no Examples menu with the dev server (the examples are written for the sample graphs).
  • New Rust items (additive): Graph::begin_unit and its closes, Graph::try_write_checked, Graph::is_poisoned, Graph::poison_cause, GraphError::StorageFailed, RollbackFailed, Poisoned, GraphViewHeld and UnitNotHeld (with constructors such as GraphError::storage_failed), GraphStorage::storage_identity and storage::StorageIdentity, GraphStorage::next_unit_started_at/begin_unit_at (defaulted), UserJobs and NotScheduledJob, RepairReport::marks_unreadable, StoreFailure::AutoCheckpointFailed, and the model API of the Store.
  • Benchmarks: the Divan bench gains mutation cases (bulk writes through traversals, small write queries through the Graph<S> lock, Rhai scripts per statement and as one unit, GQL writes).

Fixed

  • A checkpoint while a run is open no longer persists rolled-back data. A playground or dev server run kept its unit open between per-traversal locks, so a Store checkpoint taken in that window could write data the run later rolled back. Runs now hold their unit across the locks, so a checkpoint never sees a run's uncommitted changes.
  • Predicates take single values (issue #14): P.gt(["a"]) compared with the text ["a"]. Every step that takes a predicate now refuses a list, map or traversal operand with a help naming the predicate (Predicates); P.within() and P.without() without arguments are the empty set.
  • Saved queries with closures (issue #16): a closure in a saved query's body is part of its one function, and a capturing closure no longer makes a writing body dynamic.
  • define_query takes the params list get_query returns (issue #17), so get, change and define round-trip (Saved Queries).
  • Swallowed errors: a session run's commit or rollback, the Store menu's compaction advice (now compactionError), an unknown job time zone, a failed system job, the workload and memory report answers, a stored model or embedder a store cannot load, and an AI Chat saved query whose entry cannot be read (now treated as writing) report their error.
  • A storage read that fails while the engine builds the message of another error no longer replaces that error.

Performance

  • The Result of the element reads costs nothing measurable: the Divan bench of 0.4.0 against 0.3.0 is within noise overall (geometric mean -0.4 %); the glob_path() walk, which first got 4-9 % slower, reads the storage through a plain match again and is back at its 0.3.0 speed.

Format

  • No format version changes: the store format and the file format stay at version 3. Embedding models live in a new optional models/ area of a store (format spec, section 4.5) and as ignorable rows of kind 3 in a packed snapshot's segment table (section 8). Graphersal 0.3.0 opens a store with models and ignores them, loads a .gsnap with models, and refuses a ZIP backup with models as written by a newer version (make one with --without-models for it).

Project

  • Contributions are accepted under a Contributor License Agreement (Version Control and Contributions) instead of the DCO.

Breaking changes in detail

One user decision (2026-10-28) drives them: a public method that touches shared state (the graph's lock, the storage, a Store, files, embedders) returns a Result with a #[non_exhaustive] error type, even where it cannot fail today, and never answers a failure with an empty or default value.

graphersal:

  • AnyGraph (EXPERIMENTAL): capabilities() -> Result<StorageCapabilities, GraphError>, last_commit_seq() -> Result<u64, GraphError>, statistics() -> Result<Option<GraphStatistics>, GraphError>, memory_usage() -> Result<Option<MemoryStats>, GraphError>, get_schema() -> Result<Option<GraphSchema>, GraphError>, definitions(kind) -> Result<Vec<Definition>, GraphError>, definition(kind, name) -> Result<Option<Definition>, GraphError>, compression_stats(name) -> Result<Option<CompressionStats>, GraphError>, property_indexes() -> Result<Vec<PropertyIndexInfo>, GraphError> (were the plain values; a read the current thread may not have was answered as "no data", now GraphError::GraphViewHeld).

  • Graph::advise fails when a compression estimate fails for another reason than GraphError::Unsupported (was: advice without compression recommendations).

  • Store: read_only_reason() -> Result<Option<String>, PersistError>, stopped_reason() -> Result<Option<String>, PersistError>, damage_policy() -> Result<DamagePolicy, PersistError>, store_id() -> Result<u128, PersistError>, damage_found() -> Result<Vec<FoundDamage>, PersistError>, last_auto_checkpoint_error() -> Result<Option<Arc<PersistError>>, PersistError> (was Option<String>), user_jobs() -> Result<UserJobs, PersistError> (was Vec<Job>; UserJobs { jobs, not_scheduled } lists the definitions it does not schedule with the reason), stored_embedders(&registered) -> Result<StoredEmbedders, PersistError>, Store::is_store(dir) -> Result<bool, PersistError> and SingleFileDir::is_single_file(path) -> Result<bool, PersistError> (an unreadable directory or file is PersistError::Io, not false). A poisoned internal lock is StoreFailure::LockPoisoned (was a default answer).

  • Store::info (and StoreInfo everywhere) fails when the attic or the models directory cannot be read (was an empty list); a fork or attic fork fails before writing when the marks it does not carry cannot be listed.

  • GraphStorage (EXPERIMENTAL; implementers and callers): the methods beyond single elements return Result<_, GraphError> (defaults: Ok of the old default): statistics, infer_schema, get_schema, declared_property_schema, definitions (Result<impl Iterator>), definition, compression_stats, property_indexes, the four property index lookups (Result<Option<Box<dyn Iterator>>>), shrink_to_fit, memory_usage, memory_structure, memory_footprint_bytes, execution_policy, begin_unit, begin_unit_at, next_unit_started_at, rollback_unit, unit_changes, set_unit_metadata, capabilities, last_commit_seq. A failed rollback_unit still closes the unit; the engine reports GraphError::RollbackFailed.

  • Behaviour (user decision 2026-10-28): a failed rollback POISONS the Graph (was: "the graph stays usable"). When a host storage's rollback_unit (or discard_unit, other than the Unsupported of a storage without change capture) fails in any unit the engine closes on a Graph (a traversal, a transaction or dry run on a write view, an import, a change-set apply, a held unit's close, a panic unwinding through a unit), the graph refuses every later data operation with the new GraphError::Poisoned { cause } (read_checked, write_checked, try_write_checked, begin_unit, the closes of a held unit, the AnyGraph methods, sessions; try_read/try_write answer None) and Graph::read()/write() panic. No unpoison: drop the graph and reopen the storage. TraversalGraph and the Store cannot get there (their rollback cannot fail). Upgrade step for a host storage: return Err from rollback_unit only when the storage really is in an unknown state. The poison is isolated per graph: the failing storage is named by the new GraphStorage::storage_identity() -> StorageIdentity (opaque; default StorageIdentity::of(self); a wrapper over a storage held elsewhere forwards it, as the shipped wrapper impls do; the pinned clock of a held unit is now found the same way, also for Graph<Box<TraversalGraph>> and wrapper storages), so a failure never poisons another graph on the same thread, and a bare storage poisons nothing.

  • Behaviour: a storage read that fails while the engine builds the diagnostic of another error (the value origin of cast, numeric and incomparable-value errors, the type a string step, a list function or T.value names) no longer replaces that error with the storage's: the original error is reported without the unreadable detail.

  • GraphStorage, the element reads too: vertex_count/edge_count -> Result<usize, _>, vertices/edges/out_edges/in_edges -> Result<impl Iterator, _> (one Result per call, never per item), vertices_by_label/edges_by_label -> Result<Box<dyn Iterator>, _> (their defaults now collect the matches first, so a failing label read is the call's error), get_vertex_by_id/get_edge_by_id/vertex_id/edge_id/vertex_label/edge_label/ vertex_properties/edge_properties/edge_endpoints -> Result<Option<_>, _>, vertex_labels -> Result<&[CompactString], _>, vertex_has_label/contains_vertex/ contains_edge -> Result<bool, _>, unit_started_at -> Result<Option<i128>, _>. The engine fails the reading query with the error, located at its step. TraversalGraph's own inherent vertex_count()/edge_count() stay plain usize (an in-memory count that cannot fail).

  • CreateContext::for_storage and GraphStatistics::from_storage return Result<_, GraphError> (they read the storage).

  • PersistentStorage (EXPERIMENTAL): set_graph_id, raise_position, reserve_load, finish_load, clear return Result<(), GraphError>.

  • StoreDir (EXPERIMENTAL): space_usage() -> io::Result<Option<SpaceUsage>>, free_space() -> io::Result<Option<u64>>, check() -> io::Result<DirCheck>. A failing free_space fails the compaction advice (PersistError::Io) instead of reading as unknown; a failing check opens the Store in maintenance mode with that damage (as SingleFileDir did for an unreadable file).

  • GraphTraversalSource::statistics() -> TraverserResult<Option<&GraphStatistics>> and memory_usage() -> TraverserResult<Option<MemoryStats>> (were the plain values).

  • Added (not breaking): Graph::try_write_checked, UserJobs, NotScheduledJob, RepairReport::marks_unreadable, StoreFailure::AutoCheckpointFailed, GraphError::StorageFailed (GraphError::storage_failed), GraphError::RollbackFailed (GraphError::rollback_failed), GraphError::Poisoned (GraphError::poisoned), Graph::is_poisoned, Graph::poison_cause, GraphStorage::storage_identity (with a default) and storage::StorageIdentity, graphersal-storage-tests' failing::Failing (with the discard_unit, element_identity and fail_element_reads_after faults).

graphersal-session (internal, listed for the CLI and the wasm crate):

  • SessionError replaces String as the error of every public method that returned Result<_, String> (session methods, SessionGraph, GraphFactory, the generic helpers of views, filter, selection, create, edit, queries, compression, layout, advisor, store::parse_time).
  • Now Result<_, SessionError>: Session::info, statistics, get_schema, get_schema_text, infer_schema, infer_schema_text, load_shared, attach_store, list_queries, get_query, query_count, save_catalog_text, list_compressions, get_compression, compression_count, list_indexes, get_index, index_count, jobs_view, job_entry, workload_report, tick_jobs, read_only_reason.
  • SessionGraph: vertex_count, edge_count, inferred_schema, schema_view, schema_view_of, graph_view, add_degrees, statistics_view, memory_view, element, subgraph, element_view, drawn, incident_edges, queries, query, count_kind, catalog_text, compressions, compression, indexes, index, run_changes, rollback_run return Result<_, GraphError>.
  • The generic helpers over a storage's element reads return Result<_, GraphError> too: CompactGraph::build, CompactGraph::add_degrees, display::element_of (Result<Option<_>, _>), display::node_of, display::edge_of, display::collect_subgraph (Result<Option<_>, _>), views::graph_view, create::drawn_in, create::incident_edges (Result<Option<usize>, _>), edit::element_view.
  • SessionStore: read_only_reason, damage_found, damage_policy, last_auto_checkpoint_error, user_jobs return Result<_, PersistError> like Store; the trait gains models, import_models_from_packed and export_packed_with (embedding models in a Store), implemented for every Store<S>.
  • The generic helpers compressions_in, compression_in, indexes_in, index_in, queries_in, query_in, count_kind, catalog_text, views::schema_view, schema_view_of, statistics_view, memory_usage return Result<_, GraphError> (they read through the GraphStorage methods that now return one).
  • store::found_damage_value -> Result<Value, PersistError>; StoreError is #[non_exhaustive] (build it with StoreError::new, bad_request, conflict, refused, internal, with_data, or From a SessionError, PersistError or GraphError).
  • The Store menu's JSON gains compactionError (beside compaction: null when the advice cannot be computed).

graphersal-wasm (internal JS API): info, getSchema, inferSchema, schema, graphView, memoryUsage, statistics, tickJobs, jobs, listQueries, getQuery, saveCatalog, listCompressions, listIndexes throw the error instead of answering an empty value.

Python: Store.close() raises on a poisoned store lock (was "already closed"), Graph.execute raises on a poisoned limits lock (was the default limits).

Release 0.3.0

A minor release. The engine learns what its graph holds and how it is used, and acts on it: workload statistics, scheduled jobs, a memory report and a storage advisor with an Optimize panel in the playground. Dates and times reach nanosecond resolution, the in-memory graph takes markedly less memory, and the DSL spells Graphersal's own extensions in snake_case only.

It is not a drop-in update for every caller: read "Upgrading from 0.2" first.

Upgrading from 0.2

  • Graphersal's own DSL functions are snake_case only. The camelCase twins of 63 extensions are removed (createIndex, defineQuery, memoryReport, removeProperty, globPath, addLabel, setLabel, dropLabel, toJson, toTable, toMermaid, toPlantUML, firstName, dateTrunc, localDateTime, ...). TinkerPop's steps and functions keep both spellings (hasLabel and has_label), as do five names of the Java API (containsKey, isEmpty, toMap, Set.ofList, UUID.fromString). A script that still calls a removed name fails with a help that names the snake_case function (Writing Queries). Rendering in camelCase (render.spelling) keeps these names in snake_case, so the text still runs.
  • File format version 3. Every file this version writes (snapshots, journal segments, .gsnap, backups) is of format version 3, which holds the new temporal values. 0.3.0 reads every older file; 0.2.x refuses a version 3 file with a clear "unsupported version" error (never as damage). Keep a backup made by 0.2.x if you may need to go back. The store format version is unchanged (Format Versions and Upgrade).
  • Temporal values hold nanoseconds (were microseconds); see "Dates and times" below.
  • Rust API: the DT token gained DT::Nanosecond as its first unit, so the numeric values of its variants moved (only code casting a DT with as sees it; cargo-semver-checks reports nothing else). Every other change is an addition: new modules advisor, jobs and workload, new methods (Graph::advise, Graph::attach_workload_stats, memory_report, ...) and #[non_exhaustive] structs.

Added

  • Memory report (Memory and Profiling): g.memory_report() (REPL /memory, MCP memory_report, dev server POST /api/memory/report, Python memory_report()): one row per label and property with the bytes it takes, value types, a size histogram, distinct strings, what is compressed or indexed, and the structure's own share (slots, ids, labels, shapes, indexes). Sampled on large labels.
  • Workload statistics (Workload Statistics): a store counts what its queries do, per minute, hour and day (kept for 60 minutes, 48 hours and 90 days, persisted in the sidecar file WORKLOAD): queries by normalized plan (a pg_stat_statements analogue), how each property is used (filtered by a scan or an index, read, ordered, compared by similarity, written), the graph lock's wait and hold times, and the scheduled jobs; per channel (playground, MCP, CLI, Python, job, host). The playground's own drawing and panels are not counted. Read through GET /api/workload[?history=minutes|hours|days], the MCP tool workload_statistics, REPL /workload, Python workload_report(); their memory shows as workload_bytes in g.memory_usage().
  • Scheduled jobs (Scheduled Jobs): a cron scheduler the host ticks (no thread in the engine; the dev server and the browser playground tick it). System jobs (stats_flush, compact) whose schedule and switch can be changed, and jobs of users as catalog definitions (kind job): g.define_job(#{name, schedule, action, ...}) runs a saved query with fixed arguments, a checkpoint or a backup, with the definer's rights checked once and stored as the job's effects; limits per run (timeout, memory); every run recorded. Managed in the playground's Catalog ▸ Scheduled jobs, over /api/jobs*, MCP list_jobs.
  • Storage advisor and the Optimize panel (Optimize): recommendations from the memory report, the workload statistics and the catalog: create an index for a key filtered often by a full scan, drop an index no query used, compress or deduplicate large strings (savings measured on the data), stop compressing a key read often. Each names the catalog command that applies it; Apply runs it, Snooze and Dismiss hide it, and an applied one reports what it changed for 30 days. The playground's Optimize panel also shows the workload statistics as tables with sparklines and charts, and the memory report. Over HTTP /api/advise*, MCP advise, Rust Graph::advise (module graphersal::advisor).
  • Process memory in the statistics: process.memory (resident set size where the system reports it, the live heap, WebAssembly memory), loaded models and the AI Chat history, beside the graph's own footprint (playground Profile ▸ Statistics).
  • Dates and times (Dates and Times): nanosecond resolution for time, localdatetime, datetime and duration; offsettime; a zone name given to a datetime is kept; the whole java.time.Duration range; ISO GQL temporal literals and clocks; Python returns nanosecond values as pandas.Timestamp / pandas.Timedelta where pandas is installed.
  • Playground: a filter for the drawn graph (labels and property conditions), a compact Graph toolbar with a Display menu (vertex size by degree), in/out degree in the inspector, reloads throttled while the graph changes fast, shape bytes on the Statistics tab, four subgraph() examples; the Share link is hidden with the dev server (it cannot carry a server's graph).
  • OpenAPI description of the dev server's HTTP API (EXPERIMENTAL, The HTTP API): crates/graphersal-cli/openapi.json in the repository, served by graphersal --server at GET /openapi.json, its version the release's; a test keeps it in step with the router.
  • CLI and dev server: --args-file FILE / @FILE (a JSON file of arguments), --mcp-instructions FILE (operator notes in the MCP instructions); MCP answers are compact JSON, cut at whole results, with offset paging; the AI Chat accepts a custom system_prompt, reports lenient keys with hints, and shows each answer's time.

Changed

  • Less memory for the same graph. Stored property maps share their key lists (property shapes), the id index keeps no second copy of an id, vertex and edge slots are an own topology (petgraph is no longer a dependency) with interned label sets, and a load leaves no spare capacity. On the project's own knowledge graph (40k vertices, 190k edges) the graph took about half the memory of 0.2.3.
  • GQL MERGE without an index finds its match through a scan lookup, about ten times faster.
  • The MCP instructions and tool descriptions prefer GQL for reading and writing data.

Format

  • File format version 3 (format spec, section 3): new value tags for the nanosecond temporal values; versions 1 and 2 stay readable.
  • The workload statistics sidecar WORKLOAD (format spec, section 4.4, version 2): instance data, never in the journal, a snapshot or a backup; an unreadable or newer file means the statistics start anew. It also keeps the system jobs' settings and the advisor's marks.
  • Catalog kind 4: a scheduled job of a user (format spec, section 6.3).

Release 0.2.3

A patch release of the 0.2 line. GQL (still experimental) can now write, call saved queries and work with dates and times, and the playground gains GQL query tabs. It changes no format: stores, snapshots and journals of 0.2.2 are read and written exactly as before. Its API additions are additive (new methods, constants and #[non_exhaustive] error variants); three Gremlin behaviours are fixed (see "Fixed").

Added

  • GQL writes (experimental) (Writing with GQL): g.gql(query) is no longer read-only. A query is one unit: it commits as a whole or leaves nothing, and the commit hooks, the journal, schema defaults and coercion, permissions, resource limits and cancellation apply as they do to Gremlin writes.
    • INSERT (Cypher spelling CREATE) creates nodes and edges once per row; SET and REMOVE change properties and labels (n.k = e, n = map, n += map, n:A:B, REMOVE n.k); [DETACH | NODETACH] DELETE removes nodes, edges and paths; MERGE [p =] <pattern> with ON CREATE SET / ON MATCH SET finds or creates one pattern per row.
    • A query whose last clause writes may end there and returns no rows; FINISH ends any query without a result.
    • Writes run through internal steps (gql:insert_node, gql:set, gql:delete, gql:merge, ...) that ask the same permissions as their Gremlin twins; a saved query that writes is recorded with its effects.
    • Not yet: FOREACH (use FOR x IN list INSERT ...), a write inside a UNION operand, a path variable in INSERT, a nested SET / REMOVE target such as n.a.b (Not yet).
  • Saved queries written in GQL (Saved Queries): g.define_query(#{name, language: "gql", body, params}) stores a GQL query, read with $name parameters and parsed, bound and planned when it is saved. A query that reads is recorded in the dialect graphersal-gql/1, one that writes in graphersal-gql/2 with its effects (catalog::GQL_QUERY_DIALECT, catalog::GQL_WRITING_QUERY_DIALECT, QueryDefinition::language()); queries() and get_query() report language and dialect. New errors for an undeclared or unused $parameter. A version that does not know GQL saved queries (0.2.2 and older) lists them as not runnable and keeps them unchanged.
  • CALL of a saved GQL query (Calling saved queries): CALL folder.name(args) [YIELD ..], standalone or once per row inside a query (OPTIONAL CALL, YIELD .. WHERE, a VOID call may end a query). A saved query in Rhai and a call inside EXISTS / COUNT / COLLECT are not supported yet.
  • GQL dates and times (Dates in GQL, The Supported Subset): date(), local_time(), local_datetime(), datetime() and duration() (Cypher spellings localtime(), localdatetime() accepted) from ISO 8601 text, a map of fields or another temporal value; components (d.year, ...), arithmetic with durations, comparison, the clocks (.statement, .transaction; one instant per execution, inside a script the script's now()), X.truncate(unit, value), datetime.fromepoch(millis) and duration.between / inMonths / inDays / inSeconds. Values hold microseconds (finer input is refused, never cut), a zone name is turned into its offset, and zoned time() is not supported yet; every difference from Neo4j is listed on Semantics.
  • More GQL expressions and clauses: list indexing and slicing (x[i], x[a..b], m[k]), + of a list and one value, the power operator x ^ y, percentile_cont / percentile_disc, chained comparisons, a constant LIMIT / SKIP, non-reserved words as names, ORDER BY over expressions of returned aggregates, a LET / WITH value as a pattern node or edge, RETURN * in name order. Equality across kinds is FALSE, lists are ordered, float division follows IEEE 754 (NaN, Infinity). A construct that is meaningless for its operand kinds is refused with a static error. The deliberate differences from Neo4j and ISO are collected in Semantics and Conformance.
  • openCypher TCK harness (TCK Compliance): the openCypher TCK 2024.3 is vendored unmodified (crates/graphersal/tests/opencypher/, not part of the published crate) and run by cargo test --test opencypher_tck against the compatibility forms GQL accepts, with a ratchet baseline and a generated compliance page. At this release 3216 of 3818 in-scope cases pass (84.2 %, 95.7 % without the temporal group) and the wrong behaviour of supported constructs is 0; the rest is missing constructs. The kit measures the Cypher compatibility forms that GQL accepts.
  • Playground (Web Playground): query tabs can be GQL (highlighting, completion, parameters, error spans, "Save as query..." from a g.gql(..) tab), the saved-query editor has a language switch and completes the declared $parameters, the new Examples panel has search, collapsible groups and GQL subgroups (including write examples), element details collapse long values, and the panel header wraps on narrow screens. The book's GQL run buttons open GQL tabs. The MCP tool gql and the AI Chat can write (read-only under --mcp-read-only; the AI Chat only when asked), and the session reports a change summary.

Changed

  • g.gql() is no longer read-only: a query with a write clause that used to be refused now runs. A host that relied on the refusal restricts it with an Authorizer / AccessPolicy (writes ask Create, Update and Delete on Data like their Gremlin twins) or --mcp-read-only.
  • GQL answers that were wrong or too strict now follow the TCK (cross-kind equality, ordering of lists, NaN, WITH ... WHERE seeing the dropped names, and more); a query that relied on such an answer may return a different one.
  • Result JSON writes NaN, Infinity and -Infinity as GraphSON typed doubles ({"@type": "g:Double", "@value": "NaN"}) in the playground, the dev server, MCP, to_json() and --format json; they used to fail with "non-finite float cannot be represented in JSON". The strict writers (GraphML, the plain serde of a value) stay strict.

Fixed

  • where(P.eq("x")) compares by logical value (Predicates): where(P.eq(..)), where(P.neq(..)), the end label of where(__.as("x")), where(P.eq(..)).by(..) and where(P.within(..)) compared the current object with the labelled one structurally, so a computed value (inject, constant, math) never equalled a lazily read property, two properties of different elements never matched, and 1 never equalled 1.0. Scalars now compare by the rules P.eq applies to a literal, elements by identity, containers by value.
  • merge_v() and merge_e() ask Read on what they search (Permissions): they asked only Create and Update, so a policy that denied reading could still probe for existence through them. A policy that allows writes but not reads now denies them.
  • A cross product is checked against the traverser limit before it is built: MATCH (a), (b) (and a mid-traversal v()) on a large graph reserved the whole product up front and could abort the process. It now fails with memory.allocation and a Help: line when it exceeds traversal.max_traversers or the memory budget, and capacities taken from query data are capped.

Release 0.2.2

A patch release of the 0.2 line. It brings GQL read queries, marked experimental, and fixes how value filters treat a string that names a step label. It changes no format: stores, snapshots and journals of 0.2.1 are read and written exactly as before. Its API additions are additive (a new feature, new methods, a new #[non_exhaustive] error variant).

Added

  • GQL read queries (experimental) (GQL Queries): g.gql(query) runs a query in GQL, the ISO graph query language (ISO/IEC 39075), on the same graph and engine as Gremlin. The query is compiled into an ordinary traversal plan, so the optimizer, property indexes, profile(), resource limits, cancellation, permissions and custom storages apply as they do to Gremlin; each result row is a map from column name to value (Result Shape). Experimental means: gql() only reads (every write clause is refused), the supported subset grows from version to version, and the rows, errors and plans of a construct may still change in a later version. Gremlin stays the complete, stable interface.
    • Supported (The Supported Subset): MATCH and OPTIONAL MATCH, WHERE, LET, FILTER, Cypher's WITH, RETURN with aggregation, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, OFFSET/LIMIT; FOR (Cypher UNWIND) with WITH ORDINALITY/OFFSET; queries that start without MATCH; node and edge patterns, label expressions, quantified edges (-[:knows]->{1,3}) and quantified path patterns ((a) ((x)-[:created]->(s)<-[:created]-(y)){1,2} (b)), path variables (trail semantics: no edge bound twice in a match); EXISTS subqueries and Cypher pattern predicates; map projections, list and pattern comprehensions and RECORD {..} for JSON-shaped answers; Cypher's COUNT { }, COLLECT { }, all()/any()/none()/single() and reduce(); composite queries (UNION, UNION ALL, NEXT); CALL { } subqueries run per row (OPTIONAL CALL); parameters ($name); three-valued logic; the GQL scalar functions (strings, numbers, CAST) and the common openCypher ones (toInteger, substring, split, round, keys, nodes(p), ...).
    • ISO first, Cypher spellings accepted (Cypher Aliases): where GQL and Cypher differ, GQL wins; unambiguous Cypher spellings with the same meaning are accepted as aliases (SKIP, !=, toUpper(), -->, ...). There is no Graphersal-only syntax.
    • Errors (Errors): a query that does not parse or bind fails before anything runs, with a GQLSTATUS code, a caret under the offending text and a Help: line; constructs outside the subset are refused by name with an alternative (Refused Constructs). Size limits (pattern edges, subqueries, nesting) are errors, never a cut result.
    • Plans (Plans and Performance): a GQL query and its Gremlin twin get the same plan where they mean the same; profile() shows the internal gql:* steps; an equality on an indexed property and an id lookup per row are served directly.
    • Everywhere: Rust GraphTraversalSource::gql and gql_with(query, params) (feature gql, off by default, no dependencies, builds for wasm32), the Rhai DSL g.gql(query) / g.gql(query, params), the CLI and REPL, Python (graph.query("g.gql(...)")), the playground (GQL examples), and the MCP server's tool gql. New error TraverserError::Gql with GqlErrorKind.
    • Not yet: writes (INSERT, SET, DELETE, ...), EXCEPT/INTERSECT, path modes and shortest paths, a quantifier nested in a quantified path pattern (Conformance, Current Limitations).

Changed

  • A value filter compares a string as a value, never as a step label (Predicates): has(key, P.eq("a")), is("a"), has_value, their P forms, any/all/none and a jpath has compared a string that named a step label (as("a")) with the labelled element instead of the string itself, so g.v(1).as("vadas").out("knows").has("name", P.eq("vadas")) returned nothing. They now compare the literal, as TinkerPop does; only where(P) and where(P).by(..) read step labels. A traversal that relied on the old behaviour should use where(P.eq("a")). As a side effect, a property index now also serves a string P.eq inside child traversals and union() operands.
  • The profile table's Step column is as wide as the longest step text (Profiling): at least 60 characters (70 with nested steps), at most 160, then .... It was cut at 60/70, which hid annotations such as [index: ..]. The playground's Text view uses the same rule.

Release 0.2.1

Warning: do not use 0.2.0 on a store written by 0.2.1. Graphersal 0.2.0 reads a store that holds a compression rule with the codec dedup (new in 0.2.1) as damaged from the commit that defined the rule on: it opens it in maintenance mode, reports the commits from there on as lost, and graphersal store repair run from 0.2.0 would really drop them, although nothing on disk is damaged. Do not open such a store with 0.2.0 and never run graphersal store repair from 0.2.0 on it. Upgrade to 0.2.1; 0.2.0 is not recommended. From 0.2.1 on, what a newer version writes is never read as damage (see "Changed" below).

A patch release of the 0.2 line. It changes no format: stores, snapshots and journals of 0.2.0 are read and written exactly as before. Its additions are additive API (a new GraphStorage method with a default, new #[non_exhaustive] types).

Added

  • Saved queries that write (#11; Queries that read and queries that write): a saved query may now change data. Its effects (which elements of which labels it may create, update or delete) are inferred from its body when it is saved, never declared; a call asks the permission check for the whole effect set first and runs as one unit, so a failing call changes nothing. Schema, catalog and file writes, and writes the inference cannot see (behind Fn, call, eval, import or a computed query name), are refused when the query is saved. g.queries() lists writes and effects; the playground marks queries R/O or R/W and previews a writing call before it runs; the MCP server lists the effects, hides writing queries in its read-only mode, and the AI Chat runs one only after the user confirmed it. A writing query is stored in the dialect graphersal-rhai/2; read-only queries stay graphersal-rhai/1, so 0.2.0 still runs them and lists a writing one as not runnable (Unavailable queries and older versions).
  • Estimate a compression rule before defining it (#12; Estimating the gain): g.estimate_compression(#{label, path, element?, codec?, min_bytes?, dictionary?}) measures the candidate rules (lz4 without and with a dictionary at min_bytes 64 to 1024, plus the rule that covers the path today) on the current values and reports per candidate the values it would compress, plain, stored and dictionary bytes, the net saving, the ratio and the measured compression and read (decompression) speed, plus the values found at the path, how many are strings, a size histogram to choose min_bytes, the best candidate and warnings for a label that does not exist, a path without values and values that are not strings. The graph is not changed (no commit, no catalog change). The trial dictionary is built by the rule's own code, so the estimate of a candidate is what the rule holds after it is defined on the same data; above 100,000 strings or 16 MiB of text a deterministic sample is measured and extrapolated (sampled: true). It asks for Read on the label's data, so read-only policies, the MCP read-only mode and saved queries may estimate. Rust GraphTraversalSource::estimate_compression(&CompressionEstimateRequest) (graphersal::catalog; storages implement GraphStorage::estimate_compression, default Unsupported), Python Graph.estimate_compression(label, path, ...), the playground's Estimate button in the compression rule form (a table of the candidates with saving bars, the best highlighted, Use fills the form), the dev server's POST /api/compression/estimate and the MCP tool estimate_compression. The help of an out-of-range min_bytes names it.
  • A dedup codec for repeated values (#13; Deduplicating repeated values): g.define_compression(#{name, label, path, codec: "dedup"}) stores every distinct value at the rule's path once, in a table of the rule, and every element keeps only a reference. For long values repeated across many elements (file paths, URLs, addresses, category texts); strings of at most 24 bytes are stored inline and never shared (the default min_bytes of a dedup rule is 25), and dictionary: true with dedup is refused with a help that names the fix. Reads stay plain and cost nothing extra, query results never change, change sets, exports and files hold plain values (no format change: a load shares the values again). g.compressions() reports the shared values (compressed_values), distinct_values, plain and stored bytes (each distinct text once plus 32 bytes); g.memory_usage() adds deduped_values, deduped_plain_bytes and dedup_table_bytes (each shared text once, part of property_bytes). The estimate measures dedup with codec: "dedup" or codec: ["lz4", "dedup"] (exact, never sampled; per candidate distinct_values; the warning high_cardinality when the values are mostly distinct) and includes a dedup rule that covers the path today. Rust Codec::Dedup, CompressionCandidate::dedup/matching_codecs, Python define_compression(..., codec="dedup") and estimate_compression(..., codec=[...]), the playground's codec choice and dedup rows in the estimate table, the MCP tools define_compression/estimate_compression. A 0.2.0 reader cannot decode a dedup rule (it reports the definition as damage, see the warning at the top): drop dedup rules before opening a store with 0.2.0.

Changed

  • What a newer version writes is never damage (format spec 16 rule 9): content behind a valid checksum that this version cannot interpret is kept or refused, never reported as damage and never offered for a repair that would drop it.
    • A compression rule whose codec or element this version does not know, or whose path it cannot parse, is kept and written back byte for byte through every store path (journal, checkpoint, fork, backup, ZIP, repair), not applied (its values stay plain), and listed with served: false and a reason by g.compressions(), Python, the session, MCP's list_compressions and the playground (a not applied badge); g.recompress refuses it with the reason. New: CompressionDefinition::unserved_reason, codec_name, element_name.
    • A property index of an unknown element kind is handled like one of an unknown type: kept, not served, listed with the reason, refused when created (PropertyIndexDefinition::element_name).
    • A saved query whose stored parameters this version cannot read (a schema keyword of a newer version) is kept, listed with the reason and refused when called (QueryDefinition::unsupported_reason).
    • A definition of a known kind whose payload fields this version cannot read is kept opaque, byte for byte, like a definition of an unknown kind.
    • A graph schema this version cannot parse (in a snapshot or a WAL record) opens the store read-only with the reason (the data without the schema); a checkpoint, fork or repair of it is refused, a backup copies it as it is.
    • An unknown interrupted operation (INTENT), an unknown GRAPH state value and a well-formed backup archive entry this version does not know are refused as unsupported.
    • A block compressed with zstd, read by a build without the persist-zstd feature, is reported as unsupported (format spec 2.1), no longer as damage.
    • New error PersistError::UnsupportedContent (written by a newer Graphersal, not damage); graphersal store verify lists such content as a note:, not as damage.

Fixed

  • A traversal where a step takes values is refused (#9): an anonymous traversal given to an argument that takes ids, labels, property keys or values (has_value(__.is("marko")), has_label(__..), out(__..), values(__..), ...) was silently turned into a string and matched nothing. It is now an error whose help names the step that runs a traversal there. New: has(T.id, traversal) and has(T.label, traversal), as in TinkerPop.
  • g.memory_usage() counts the hash index of every map. It counted a property map, a nested object, a value map and the id and label indexes by their entries only and missed the hash table beside them, so property_bytes and index_bytes were 10-20 % low. They now match the bytes the allocator measures (the large sample graph: 74.2 MiB before, 92.0 MiB now). Nothing grew: the figure was wrong, not the memory.

Release 0.2.0

The second minor release of Graphersal. It brings date and time values, property indexes, schema defaults that are applied when an element is created, and vectors with exact similarity search and embedders that turn text into vectors inside the engine (a built-in one, Model2Vec models and your own, for GraphRAG). It changes the storage format and a few APIs: read Breaking changes and the upgrade guide before you move a store or a storage implementation to it. What 0.2.0 does not do yet is on Current Limitations.

Highlights

  • Dates and times (#3; Dates and Times): five value types modelled on PostgreSQL and the SQL standard, datetime (an instant with its UTC offset), localdatetime, date, time and duration (months, days and microseconds kept apart, like interval), with microsecond resolution over the years -9999 to 9999. Time zones come from the bundled IANA database (Time Zones): date_add and date_trunc in a zone, at_zone, as_local, daylight-saving gaps and overlaps resolved as PostgreSQL does. Calendar-correct arithmetic (date_add, date_diff, age), truncation and parts, conversions, now() and today() (one time per script or unit), comparison and sorting, and the schema formats date-time, date, local-date-time, time and duration with formatMinimum/formatMaximum (Dates in a Schema). TinkerPop's datetime(), asDate(), dateAdd(), dateDiff() and DT behave as TinkerPop 3.8 specifies them (TinkerPop Compatibility). Dates are values in Rust, Rhai, Python (datetime objects and graphersal.Interval), GraphSON (the java.time types), the persistence format and the playground's editors (Storage and Exchange). A string that looks like a date stays a string: a date comes from a constructor, a conversion, a schema declaration or a typed value, never from guessing.
  • Property indexes (#4; Property Indexes): g.create_index(..) declares an ordered index on a label's top-level property; the new optimizer rule property_index answers has() equality, P.within and range filters from it (.profile() shows [index: ..]), with the same results as a scan. The declaration is stored in the catalog and travels with the graph; the entries are rebuilt at every load. Every index has a type: memory-ordered is the one type of 0.2 (an index type a later version adds is kept and listed as not served, never misread), and an index on a key the schema declares as a vector, list or map is refused with a clear message (Index types). An index may carry the transform to_lower for case-insensitive search: it keys the lowered text of string values and serves has("name", __.to_lower().is("alice")) (equality, P.within, ranges; default name <label>_<key>_to_lower; a plain index on the same key coexists) (Case-insensitive search). Python Graph.create_index (transform=), the playground's Catalog ▸ Property indexes, the dev server's /api/indexes and MCP tools.
  • has(key, traversal) follows TinkerPop: has("name", __.to_lower().is("alice")) is filter(values("name").to_lower().is("alice")) (the child runs on the property's value; an element without the property is filtered out), also with a jpath key and in the three-argument form has(label, key, traversal). Before, the anonymous traversal was silently compared as a string and matched nothing. Rust has_traversal(key, traversal).
  • Schema defaults on create (#5; Defaults on create): a schema's default now has SQL DEFAULT semantics on a label's top-level properties, and the new keyword defaultFunction fills uuidv4, uuidv7 (time-ordered, RFC 9562), now or today. add_v/add_e, mergeV/mergeE on create and the playground's create dialog fill every missing default before the element is checked, in mode open and closed; explicit values (null too) win, and existing data is never changed.
  • Vectors (Vectors): a value type for embeddings with f32, f16, i8 (scalar quantization) and bit components, up to 65 536 of them; vector([..]), as_vector(), quantize(kind), GType.VECTOR, and the schema form {"type": "array", "format": "vector", "element": .., "dimension": .., "metric": ..}, which coerces a list of numbers on write and can store a property quantized from the start. Exact search with similarity(), nearest() and vector_mean() over cosine, dot product, L2 and Hamming, combined freely with graph steps (filtered search, GraphRAG, recommendations). Vectors are values in Python (graphersal.Vector, also from a numpy array), the playground, GraphSON, GraphML (through the schema) and the persistence format. Embeddings and Vector Search walks through it, in the playground without a model and from Python with one, and the playground's Examples have an Embeddings (vectors) group.
  • Embedders (Vectors): the step embed() / embed(key) and the function embed(text) turn text into vectors through the embedders the host registered (g.embedders() lists them); the built-in hash-ngram/1 (hashed words and character n-grams: fuzzy, lexical similarity, no model file, the same bits on every target) is always there, also in the browser playground. Hosts plug in their own Embedder (a Rust trait with batching and cancellation) through Embedders::builder() and GraphTraversalSource::with_embedders, the script entry points or the session; each embedder carries a stable model identity besides its registry name. Running an embedder is Execute on the new permission resource Embedder. A computed vector is stored as a plain value: replay, recovery and loads never call an embedder.
  • Embedding a property and text queries (Vectors): the job g.embed_property(#{label, from, to, ..}) embeds a property of many elements page by page, without holding the graph's lock while the embedder runs (a concurrent writer goes on; a text changed meanwhile is skipped), restartable with only_missing; Rust Graph::embed_property / EmbedJob::run_in. The vector schema keyword embedder records per label and property which model produced the vectors; the job needs an attached schema (mode open or closed), declares the property or its embedder in the unit of its first page, and refuses another model or dimension (another element kind is quantized on write). nearest(key, "text", k) and similarity(key, "text") then take the query as text and embed it with the registered embedder of the declared model, once per execution. diff_schema reports an embedder change as embedder_changed.
  • Real embedding models: Model2Vec (Embeddings): graphersal embed-model download <repo> fetches a Model2Vec static embedding model from Hugging Face (SHA-256 checked, a manifest beside it; the only network access of the tool) and embed-model list shows the downloaded ones; --embedder NAME=PATH|REPO and --default-embedder NAME register a model for every mode (one-shot, REPL, dev server, MCP, AI Chat tools), run locally on the CPU. Its model identity is model2vec/<repo>@<hash of the files>, never a path. In Rust it is graphersal::vector::Model2Vec behind the new feature model2vec (off by default, native only, loads from a local directory only); the CLI has it on by default.
  • Embedders in Python (Python Quick Start: Embedders): graphersal.Embedder(name, fn, dimension=..) makes any Python model an embedder (fn(texts) returns the rows or one 2-D numpy array, read without a numpy dependency), and graphersal.Model2Vec(name, path, model="minishlab/potion-base-8M") loads a Model2Vec model from a directory the developer downloaded (the library never downloads; the identity equals the command line's download of the same files). Every graph constructor, loader and Store opener takes embedders=[..] and default_embedder=; graph.register_embedder, graph.embedders() and graph.embed_property(label=.., source=.., target=..) (GIL released, Ctrl+C cancels between pages, EmbedPropertyError.report on failure) complete it, and scripts and text queries use the registry. Rust: Embedders::scope gives the script entry points that build their own engine a host's registry, Model2VecOptions::with_repo names the repository of a host-downloaded model.
  • Playground: the schema editor's tables edit defaultFunction and a vector's element, dimension, metric and embedder; the Graph and Mermaid drawings always show the schema the tables show (also a draft); the Mermaid diagram parses whatever labels and property names hold; the Detailed drawing zooms by mouse wheel as fast as the Fast one; a click on a panel's title collapses it; the header shows the engine version and the build.
  • Properties named id or label (#1; Properties Named id or label) are read as properties, never as the element's id or label, and vertices and edges returned by a terminal are values with their id, label and properties apart (#2; Vertices and Edges as Values).
  • Store upgrade: graphersal store upgrade (Rust Store::upgrade, Python Store.upgrade) converts a store, backup or single-file store of 0.1.x to the 0.2 format with this binary alone, keeping the whole history (Format Versions and Upgrade).
  • Files of a newer Graphersal are refused, never taken for damage (#6), as in 0.1.1; which older versions are upgraded, and how, is one table in the code, shown on Format Versions and Upgrade.
  • Prebuilt binaries (Installation): every release has archives of the graphersal command-line tool for Linux (x86_64, aarch64), macOS (Apple silicon, Intel) and Windows (x86_64), with SHA256SUMS and GitHub build-provenance attestations; cargo binstall graphersal-cli installs them. The Linux binaries are statically linked with musl and run on any distribution, but are slower on allocation-heavy queries than a source build (Performance of the prebuilt Linux binaries).

TinkerPop conformance

The vendored Apache TinkerPop 3.8.2 suite: 1631 of 1675 in-scope scenarios pass (97.4 %, 0.1.x: 1599, 95.5 %), 39 are unsupported (0.1.x: 71) and 0 supported steps behave differently from the specification. The date and time features (DateTime, AsDate, DateAdd, DateDiff) pass completely; the remaining gaps are mainly call() and the set type (TinkerPop Compliance).

Breaking changes

0.2.0 is a minor release before 1.0 and may break the 0.1 API (Releases and Versioning). Every break, and what to do:

Stored data and files

  • Store format version 3, file format version 2. 0.2.0 writes new snapshot, WAL and packed snapshot files of file format version 2 (the value tags of the date and time types and of vectors) and marks its stores with store format version 3. It reads every 0.1.x file as it is: a .gsnap of 0.1.x loads unchanged. A store of 0.1.x (store format version 2) is refused with OlderFormat until it is upgraded once with graphersal store upgrade (below); nothing is changed until you do.
  • There is no way back. An upgraded store, and every store or file 0.2.0 writes, is refused by 0.1.x. 0.1.1 refuses it cleanly as "written by a newer Graphersal" in every operation. 0.1.0 does not: it refuses to open such a store, but store info calls it corrupt, store verify lists damage, and a newer snapshot or WAL file can make it open a store in maintenance mode and offer a repair that loses data. Replace 0.1.0 with 0.1.1 wherever a 0.2 store or backup may be seen by an older binary.

Behaviour

  • A schema's default is applied. In 0.1.x default was an annotation only. Now a top-level default of a label is stored when an element is created without that property, in mode open and closed. Check the schemas you keep before you upgrade: remove a default that was only meant as documentation, or move it into description. set_schema, patch_schema and validate_schema now refuse a default that is not a valid value of its property (a stored schema with one still loads, but creating an element would then fail its check: run g.validate_schema(g.get_schema())). diff_schema reports default_changed.
  • Vertices and edges returned as values (#2). to_list()/next() return VertexValue/EdgeValue in Rust, Vertex/Edge in Rhai and graphersal.Vertex/graphersal.Edge in Python, instead of a flat map of id, label and properties. Read v.id, v.label and v["name"] (Python: v.id, v.label, v["name"]), v.properties for the map. The JSON form (playground, MCP, to_json()) is untyped GraphSON 3: a vertex {id, label, properties}, an edge {id, label, inVLabel, outVLabel, inV, outV, properties}; _from/_to are gone (use outV/inV). g.inject(v) of an element value emits the stored element and asks the authorizer for Read on Data.
  • id and label as property names (#1). by("label")/by("id") read a property, as in TinkerPop: use by(T.label)/by(T.id) for the element's own. select("id")/select("label") on an elementMap()/valueMap(true) result read a property only: use select(T.id)/select(T.label). An edge's elementMap() has Direction.OUT/Direction.IN entries.
  • GraphSON converts dates instead of skipping them. g:Date, g:Timestamp, gx:Instant, gx:OffsetDateTime, gx:ZonedDateTime (zone id dropped, reported), gx:LocalDate, gx:LocalDateTime, gx:LocalTime, gx:Duration and gx:Period become date and time values; 0.1.x skipped them, so the same file now yields properties that were absent before. A date-time text without an offset is refused, never read as UTC. The export writes the java.time tags (GraphSON).

API for storage implementers (EXPERIMENTAL)

  • insert_* is the storage primitive, add_* applies defaults (#5). The required GraphStorage methods are renamed: implement insert_vertex/insert_edge (formerly add_vertex/add_edge, same arguments), which store exactly what they are given. add_vertex/add_edge are now provided methods that fill the schema's create-time defaults and then call insert_*; do not override them. add_vertex_with/add_edge_with take a CreateContext (graphersal::storage: the time now/today store, from CreateContext::for_storage) and are the one override point per kind. Code that copies or replays data (imports, apply_change_set, recovery) calls insert_*. TraversalGraph::add_vertex/add_edge apply defaults too; insert_vertex/insert_edge are added. graphersal-storage-tests has the new item add_applies_schema_defaults_insert_does_not.
  • New provided trait methods (defaults keep a storage compiling): property_indexes() and the index lookups, unit_started_at(); StorageCapabilities::property_indexes; MemoryStats::property_index_bytes.
  • ElementProperty and ValueType have new variants (dates, vectors), and ElementProperty::Vertex/Edge carry VertexValue/EdgeValue. Downstream matches need a _ arm, as the enums are #[non_exhaustive].

Upgrading from 0.1.x

  1. Replace any 0.1.0 binary with 0.1.1 on machines that may meet an upgraded store or backup (see There is no way back).
  2. Back up the store with 0.1.x while it is closed: graphersal store backup my_store/ backup_0_1/ (or a copy of the closed directory or .gstore file).
  3. Upgrade it with 0.2.0, into a new store (the old one is only read): graphersal store upgrade my_store/ my_store_0_2/, or in place: graphersal store upgrade my_store/ --in-place. The store is verified first; everything is carried, history, marks, attic and creation parameters included, and only GRAPH is rewritten. A backup directory stays a backup (store upgrade old_backup/ new_backup/), a ZIP backup is upgraded as it is restored (store restore old_backup.zip new_store/). In Python: graphersal.Store.upgrade("my_store", "my_store_0_2") or in_place=True. Details: Format Versions and Upgrade and store upgrade.
  4. Review the stored schema's defaults (above): graphersal --graph my_store_0_2/ -e 'g.validate_schema(g.get_schema())'.
  5. Update code that reads returned elements: maps become Vertex/Edge values; by("label") becomes by(T.label) where the element's label is meant. In Python, result["name"] keeps working on a graphersal.Vertex, while result["id"]/result["label"] now read properties (a KeyError when there is none): use result.id/result.label.
  6. GraphSON files with java.time values now import them as dates; a query that relied on their absence, or a schema that declared them as string, needs a look. Packed snapshots (.gsnap) of 0.1.x need no step.
  7. Storage implementers: rename add_vertex/add_edge to insert_vertex/insert_edge, pin graphersal = "=0.2.0" and graphersal-storage-tests = "=0.2.0", and run the conformance suite (Custom Storages).

Dependencies

  • jiff (time zone rules and the bundled IANA database; the only new dependency of the default build).
  • Feature model2vec only: model2vec-rs (MIT), tokenizers (Apache-2.0, with the pure-Rust fancy-regex backend: no C or C++ code) and safetensors (Apache-2.0), with their own dependencies (ndarray, half, rayon, fancy-regex, ...). The CLI's embed-model download uses the ureq client it already has and ring (already in its tree through rustls) for SHA-256.
  • rustls 0.23.46 and ruzstd at least 0.9.1 (RustSec advisories), as in 0.1.1.

Compatibility

  • Minimum supported Rust version: 1.88.
  • Python 3.10+ (abi3 wheels).
  • Versioning and what is stable in 0.2.x: Releases and Versioning.

Release 0.1.1

A patch release of the 0.1 line. It changes no format and no API; valid stores, snapshots and journals of 0.1.0 are read and written exactly as before.

Fixed

  • Files of a newer Graphersal are refused, never taken for damage (#6). 0.1.0 refused a store whose GRAPH file has a newer store format version only when it opened it; graphersal store info read the snapshot manifests first and called such a store corrupt, store verify listed DAMAGE, and a store whose snapshot or WAL files carried a newer file format version opened in maintenance mode and offered a repair that would have lost data. Now every operation (open, read-only open, info, verify, the damage report, repair, fork, checkpoint, backup into or from it, restore incl. ZIP, prune, convert, the attic commands, listings and exports; the CLI, the dev server and Python alike) refuses a store, backup or single-file store with a newer GRAPH (either copy), a newer snapshot manifest, snapshot segment or WAL segment anywhere in it (the attic too), or a newer single-file container, with PersistError::UnsupportedVersion ("written by a newer Graphersal"), before it takes a lock, reads data or writes anything. A packed snapshot or journal stream of a newer file format version is refused the same way. The rule is in the format specification, section 15 and on Format Versions.

Dependencies

  • rustls 0.23.46 in the lock file (RUSTSEC-2026-0346, -0347, -0348 and a ServerHello downgrade advisory; used only by the CLI's AI Chat client, --ai).
  • ruzstd at least 0.9.1 (RUSTSEC-2026-0344, a decompression bomb; used only with the feature persist-zstd, whose chunk sizes are bounded before decoding).

Release 0.1.0

The first public release of Graphersal: an in-memory graph traversal engine in Rust, modelled on Apache TinkerPop Gremlin, with a durable store, a command line, a Python binding and a browser playground. What 0.1.0 does not do yet is on Current Limitations.

The engine and the query language

  • Gremlin traversals in Rust and in a Rhai script DSL, in both spellings (has_label and hasLabel), with a rule-based optimizer, bulk traversers, sacks, repeat() loops, upserts (mergeV/mergeE), math(), nested property paths (jpath), UUID values and multi-label vertices.
  • TinkerPop conformance: the vendored Apache TinkerPop 3.8.2 Gherkin suite runs on every test run. More than 95 % of the in-scope scenarios pass and no supported step behaves differently from the specification; the numbers and every deliberate difference are on TinkerPop Compliance and TinkerPop Deviations.
  • Every traversal is atomic: a failing traversal leaves nothing behind; explicit transactions, dry runs, change capture and commit hooks are in the Rust API (Transactions).
  • Profiling of the optimized plan with timings, traverser counts and optional exact memory figures; execute() returns results, error and profile of one run without throwing.
  • Schemas: one format everywhere (a strict subset of JSON Schema 2020-12 per label), enforced in open or closed mode, inferred from data, diffed and patched; a schema change is a database change.
  • Saved queries and compressed properties live in a catalog stored with the graph.
  • Safe for untrusted queries: resource limits, an optional memory budget, cancellation, and a pluggable authorizer; no query may crash the engine (a fuzzer checks it).

Data in and out

  • GraphSON 3.0 import and export (TinkerGraph reads the export), and GraphML with logical types restored from a stored schema.
  • Persistence: lossless packed snapshots, a write-ahead journal and the Store: one directory (or one file) per graph with recovery on open, checkpoints, marks, point-in-time reads, fork, rollback with an attic, verified full and incremental backups, verify, damage detection with a read-only maintenance mode and repair. The format is a public specification.

Front ends

  • Command line graphersal: a REPL with completion and help, a scriptable one-shot runner with bounded display and exit codes, and graphersal store to operate stores (Command Cheat Sheet).
  • Web playground: the real engine compiled to WebAssembly, with a graph drawing, a schema editor, saved queries, a store in memory and Share link (a query and a small graph in one link, for example in a bug report); the same UI runs over the dev server (graphersal --server), which can also serve MCP to AI clients and an experimental AI Chat.
  • Python: the graphersal package (abi3 wheels for Python 3.10+) with graphs, schemas and the Store (Python).

For integrators

  • The GraphStorage trait lets a host run the engine, the DSL, saved queries and the Store over its own storage (Custom Storages); graphersal-storage-tests checks an implementation (Storage Conformance). Both are experimental in 0.1.x.

Compatibility

  • Minimum supported Rust version: 1.88.
  • Versioning and what is stable in 0.1.x: Releases and Versioning.
  • Date and time values and the TinkerPop date steps are planned for 0.2.0.
